previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure (EF 25%), chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and prior AAA repair was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and constipation over three days, along with acute kidney injury. Initial labs showed elevated creatinine (1.7) from a baseline of 1.3, prompting discontinuation of furosemide and lisinopril. CT imaging revealed non-specific jejunal wall thickening, likely due to constipation or mild enteritis, with no surgical pathology. The patient was treated with a bowel regimen including Miralax, senna, docusate, and bisacodyl, leading to symptom resolution. Kidney function improved to baseline (Cr 1.2), and furosemide was restarted at a reduced dose (40mg daily). Lisinopril was held for outpatient restart. INR was therapeutic (2.3) on warfarin for a known ventricular thrombus, and Lovenox was discontinued. Transaminitis (ALT 78, AST 67) showed improvement and was attributed to medication effects. The patient was discharged home with a bowel regimen, follow-up labs, and PCP coordination for medication management.
